sentences.en: So, Ben, we have always turned to you to explain to us in your very wise and plain-spoken way what's actually happening with our economy.
sentences.zh: 那么，本，我们总是向你求助，请你用你那非常睿智、通俗易懂的方式向我们解释我们的经济到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, in the simplest terms, what is happening in the American economy at this very moment?
sentences.zh: 那么，用最简单的话来说，此时此刻美国经济正在发生什么？

sentences.en: So, I think to put it very simply, the economy is pretty good right now, and Americans feel terrible about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得简而言之，现在经济相当不错，而美国人对此感觉糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Which is what we call in journalism a contradiction.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们在新闻界所说的矛盾。

sentences.en: It's a bit of a conundrum.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人费解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, let's pick that conundrum, contradiction apart.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来剖析这个谜题和矛盾。

sentences.en: What is the evidence that the economy is doing well?
sentences.zh: 有什么证据表明经济表现良好？

sentences.en: What data support that claim?
sentences.zh: 什么数据支持这种说法？

sentences.en: So, look, whenever we're thinking about the economy, we've got to say relative to what?
sentences.zh: 所以，看，每当我们在思考经济时，我们都得问：跟什么比？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Relative to pre-pandemic, things are okay.
sentences.zh: 与大流行前相比，情况还可以。

sentences.en: Relative to the worst moments of the pandemic a year and a half ago, things look far better than any of us could have anticipated.
sentences.zh: 与一年半前大流行最糟糕的时期相比，情况比我们任何人预期的都要好得多。

sentences.en: We've regained something like 80% of the jobs that we lost in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们已经恢复了在大流行中失去的工作岗位的 80% 左右。

sentences.en: That's a lot.
sentences.zh: 这可不少。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate is down to 4.6%.
sentences.zh: 失业率已经下降到 4.6%。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: People are making more money and spending more money than they ever have before, not just in the pandemic, but ever, ever.
sentences.zh: 人们赚钱和花钱的金额都超过了以往任何时候，不仅超过了大流行期间，而且是史无前例。

sentences.en: Ever in the history of the economy.
sentences.zh: 经济史上的空前水平。

sentences.en: Ever in the history of the economy.
sentences.zh: 经济史上的空前水平。

sentences.en: People are seeing strong wage gains by a lot of the sort of traditional measures that we use to ask how the economy is doing.
sentences.zh: 通过我们用来询问经济表现的许多传统指标来看，人们看到了强劲的工资增长。

sentences.en: It's coming back quickly and doing pretty well.
sentences.zh: 它正在迅速恢复并且表现相当不错。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: That's an even happier portrait of economic good news than I would have imagined.
sentences.zh: 这比我能想象的关于经济好消息的描绘还要令人高兴。

sentences.en: So, let's zero in on the second half of the contradiction you articulated, which is that people are feeling bad about the economy.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们把镜头对准你所阐述的矛盾的后半部分，也就是人们对经济感到悲观。

sentences.en: What is the evidence for that, given the pretty happy-sounding economy you just described?
sentences.zh: 鉴于你刚刚描述的那个听起来相当不错的经济状况，这方面的证据是什么？

sentences.en: On a basic level, we asked people.
sentences.zh: 从最基本的层面来说，我们问过人们。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, we have all of these surveys that have been going on for, in some cases, decades, asking Americans how they feel about the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有所有这些已经持续了有时几十年的调查，询问美国人对经济的感受。

sentences.en: The University of Michigan runs a long-running survey of consumer sentiment.
sentences.zh: 密歇根大学长期开展一项消费者信心调查。

sentences.en: By that measure, in early November, Americans feeling about the economy was the worst in a decade.
sentences.zh: 通过该指标，在 11 月初，美国人对经济的感受达到十年来的最低谷。

sentences.en: That means they felt worse about the economy now than they did in the worst moments of the pandemic in the spring of 2020.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们现在对经济的感受比 2020 年春季大流行最糟糕时期还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Which is confusing.
sentences.zh: 这很令人困惑。

sentences.en: I mean, we had an unemployment rate that was close to 15%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当时的失业率接近 15%。

sentences.en: We had an economy, Ben, that was shut down.
sentences.zh: 本，当时我们的经济是停摆的。

sentences.en: That was shut down.
sentences.zh: 是停摆的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People felt better about the economy then than they do now.
sentences.zh: 人们当时对经济的感觉比现在还要好。

sentences.en: The Gallup poll has run this survey for a long time.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普民意测验进行这项调查已经有很长时间了。

sentences.en: They found 68% of Americans say that the economy is getting worse right now, even though 74% say that it's a good time to find a quality job.
sentences.zh: 他们发现 68% 的美国人表示目前经济正在恶化，尽管 74% 的人表示现在是找到好工作的好时机。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, they say, I can go get a good job right now, but I still think the economy is going down the tubes.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们说，我现在可以去找一份好工作，但我仍然认为经济在走下坡路。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And 68%, nearly 70% of people thinking the economy is going down the tubes, is just an overwhelming majority of people being surveyed.
sentences.zh: 68% 的人，将近 70% 的人认为经济在走下坡路，这只是接受调查的人中的绝大多数。

sentences.en: It's the kind of number that we don't see in a lot of places.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在很多地方都看不到的数字。

sentences.en: You can't get Americans to agree on that kind of thing with any regularity.
sentences.zh: 你无法让美国人以任何规律性就这种事情达成一致。

sentences.en: Now, I do want to be clear here, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我在这里要明确一点，对吧？

sentences.en: There is a strong partisan component to what we're seeing.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的现象有一个强烈的党派成分。

sentences.en: And to some extent, this started as a partisan phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这最初是一个党派现象。

sentences.en: The moment that Joe Biden took office,
sentences.zh: 在乔·拜登就职的那一刻起，

sentences.en: confidence among Republicans plummeted.
sentences.zh: 共和党人的信心急剧下降。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Their guy had lost, so they didn't like the economy of the guy who won.
sentences.zh: 他们支持的人输了，所以他们不喜欢获胜者的经济政策。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And confidence among Democrats rose.
sentences.zh: 民主党人的信心上升了。

sentences.en: But the recent decline that we've seen is bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 但我们最近看到的下降是跨党派的。

sentences.en: Democrats, independents, Republicans, they're all saying that things have taken a turn for the worse over the last few months.
sentences.zh: 民主党人、独立人士、共和党人，他们都说过去几个月情况在恶化。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, just to summarize, the people really do feel the economy isn't going great data.
sentences.zh: 所以，简单总结一下，人们确实觉得经济没有好转的数据。

sentences.en: It's, according to public polling, real.
sentences.zh: 根据公众民意调查，这是真实的。

sentences.en: It's widespread and it's bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 它是广泛存在的，并且是跨党派的。

sentences.en: More Republican than Democrat, but now spread across both parties.
sentences.zh: 共和党人比民主党人多，但现在已经蔓延到两个党派。

sentences.en: So, Ben, how do you explain why this pessimism about the economy is so pervasive when the economic data that you just laid out suggests in reality it's quite good?
sentences.zh: 那么，本，你如何解释为什么这种对经济的悲观情绪如此普遍，而你刚才列出的经济数据却表明现实中它相当不错？

sentences.en: Why do people feel like they're being rained upon when it's actually pretty sunny out?
sentences.zh: 为什么明明外面阳光明媚，人们却觉得自己正挨雨淋？

sentences.en: So, I think there are really two reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为实际上有两个原因。

sentences.en: The first one is inflation.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是通货膨胀。

sentences.en: We are seeing a moment right now where consumer prices are rising at their fastest rate in more than 30 years.
sentences.zh: 我们目前看到消费者价格正以 30 多年来最快的速度上涨。

sentences.en: Consumer prices were up more than 6% in October from a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 10 月份消费者价格比去年同期上涨了 6% 以上。

sentences.en: And just to make clear what that actually looks like, if something was supposed to be $100,
sentences.zh: 为了明确这到底是什么样子，如果某样东西原本应该是 100 美元，
现在则是 106 美元。

sentences.en: It's real money.
sentences.zh: 这是真金白银。

sentences.en: It's real money.
sentences.zh: 这是真金白银。

sentences.en: It's not, as a one-time standalone thing, that huge.
sentences.zh: 作为一个一次性的独立事件，这并不是那么巨大。

sentences.en: But if that continues over time, right, that starts to have a real impact on people's lives.
sentences.zh: 但如果这种情况随着时间推移持续下去，对吧，那就会开始对人们的生活产生真正的冲击。

sentences.en: And look, there are some things that are rising much faster.
sentences.zh: 而且看，有些东西涨得更快。

sentences.en: Gas prices are up nearly 50% over the last year.
sentences.zh: 过去一年汽油价格上涨了近 50%。

sentences.en: Now, that's partly because gas prices fell a lot in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 现在，这部分是因为汽油价格在大流行期间大幅下跌。

sentences.en: But still, if you were paying $2 and something for gas a year ago, you're paying $3 and something, in some cases $3.50 or $4 in some parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，如果你一年前加油花的是 2 美元多，现在你得花 3 美元多，在某些地方甚至达到了 3.50 美元或 4 美元。

sentences.en: That's a price that you probably pay all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你可能一直在付的价钱。

sentences.en: And it's a price you see on the highway every time you drive down it.
sentences.zh: 这是你在公路上每次开车都能看到的价钱。

sentences.en: You're super aware of it.
sentences.zh: 你对此超级敏感。

sentences.en: Car prices.
sentences.zh: 汽车价格。

sentences.en: You know, I think back in the spring, we talked about how used car prices had jumped 10% in just one month, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想起在春天的时候，我们讨论过二手车价格在一个月内就飙升了 10%，对吧？

sentences.en: So a car that cost $20,000 in April cost $22,000 just a month later.
sentences.zh: 所以一辆在 4 月份价值 20,000 美元的车，仅仅一个月后就价值 22,000 美元了。

sentences.en: Well, now that car would cost $26,000.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在那辆车要 26,000 美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Same car.
sentences.zh: 同一辆车。

sentences.en: Same car, on average, would now cost, you know, substantially more.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，同一辆车现在要贵得多。

sentences.en: Price of food is up significantly.
sentences.zh: 食品价格大幅上涨。

sentences.en: Price of chicken and pork are up.
sentences.zh: 鸡肉和猪肉价格都在上涨。

sentences.en: Staples that people buy time after time.
sentences.zh: 人们一次又一次购买的生活必需品。

sentences.en: You're going to have to buy food in some form or fashion.
sentences.zh: 你总得以某种形式购买食物。

sentences.en: You're going to have to buy gas if you want to get to work.
sentences.zh: 如果你想去上班，你就得买汽油。

sentences.en: These are things that people pay frequently that they can't get out of.
sentences.zh: 这些是人们频繁支付且无法避开的费用。

sentences.en: And they are rising by substantial amounts.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的涨幅相当大。

sentences.en: So introduce us to the kind of person whose experience with inflation is making them feel
sentences.zh: 给我们介绍一下这样一类人：他们在通货膨胀中的经历

sentences.en: worse about the economy, even if they're benefiting from the positive forces that you described at the start of our conversation.
sentences.zh: 让他们对经济感到更加悲观，即使他们正受益于我们在对话之初谈到的那些积极因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think that question actually highlights a really important point, which is that we're
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这个问题实际上点出了一个非常重要的观点，那就是我们在

sentences.en: having this conversation in the aggregate, but people don't experience the economy that way, right?
sentences.zh: 从宏观层面讨论这个问题，但人们并不是以这种方式体验经济的，对吧？

sentences.en: They experience it in very specific terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们是以非常具体的方式感受到的。

sentences.en: And there are plenty of people out there who are not doing better.
sentences.zh: 而且有相当多的人，他们的生活并没有变得更好。

sentences.en: So, you know, imagine somebody who's got, you know, maybe it's a middle class family in Pennsylvania, got a long way to drive to work every day.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，想象一下某个家庭，比方说宾夕法尼亚州的一个中产阶级家庭，每天开车通勤要走很远的路。

sentences.en: Maybe the parents have gotten small raises this year, but not as much as inflation.
sentences.zh: 也许这对父母今年得到了小幅加薪，但幅度赶不上通货膨胀。

sentences.en: They drive a lot, so they're paying more for gas.
sentences.zh: 他们开车很多，所以支付的油费更高了。

sentences.en: Maybe they needed to replace one of the cars, so they had to buy that car that suddenly costs more money.
sentences.zh: 也许他们需要换掉其中一辆车，所以他们不得不买那辆突然变得更贵的车。

sentences.en: They've got a couple of kids, and so their grocery bills are high, and they're experiencing that.
sentences.zh: 他们有几个孩子，所以他们的食品杂货开销很大，他们正在经历这一切。

sentences.en: That family could very well be dealing with higher prices that are rising faster than any wage growth that they're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭很有可能正在面对上涨速度超过他们任何工资增长的更高物价。

sentences.en: They could be sliding backwards.
sentences.zh: 他们的生活水平可能会在倒退。

sentences.en: So for that family, right, there's not really any conundrum here at all.
sentences.zh: 所以对这个家庭来说，这里其实根本没有什么费解的谜团。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But then there are these other people who are experiencing wage growth.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，还有另一群人正在经历工资增长。

sentences.en: Interestingly, right now, wages for the lowest earning workers are the ones that are rising the fasteSt.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，现在收入最低的工人群体，他们的工资涨幅反而是最大的。

sentences.en: Retail workers.
sentences.zh: 零售业工人。

sentences.en: Retail workers, restaurant workers, right?
sentences.zh: 零售业工人，餐饮业工人，对吧？

sentences.en: Everybody where you hear, oh, we can't find workers, well, they're raising pay right now.
sentences.zh: 在所有你听到“哦，我们找不到工人”的地方，他们现在都在提高薪酬。

sentences.en: So those workers are seeing wage growth that is definitely faster than inflation.
sentences.zh: 所以这些工人看到的工资增长绝对比通货膨胀要快。

sentences.en: In a straight dollars and cents world, they are doing better now than they were a year ago.
sentences.zh: 在一个纯粹凭真金白银说话的世界里，他们现在的状况比一年前要好。

sentences.en: And so are they feeling better?
sentences.zh: 那他们的感觉是不是也更好了呢？

sentences.en: Not necessarily, right?
sentences.zh: 未必，对吧？

sentences.en: Some of this is the psychology of inflation.
sentences.zh: 这里面有一部分是通货膨胀的心理学效应。

sentences.en: You see the prices going up, and you say, well, I got a raise this year, but am I going to get a raise next year?
sentences.zh: 你看到物价上涨，然后你就会想，嗯，我今年加薪了，但我明年还能加薪吗？

sentences.en: And if prices keep going up like this, are my wages going to keep up with that?
sentences.zh: 如果物价继续这样上涨，我的工资能跟得上吗？

sentences.en: So even if in real dollar terms, this theoretical person we're talking about has more money than they did before, they're starting to experience a creeping fear that if chicken
sentences.zh: 所以，即使按实际美元计算，我们谈论的这个理论上的人物拥有的钱比以前更多了，但他们开始产生一种潜滋暗长的恐惧：如果鸡肉、

sentences.en: and beef and used car prices keep creeping up over time, that raise gets erased.
sentences.zh: 牛肉和二手车的价格随着时间不断上涨，那点加薪就会被抹平。

sentences.en: I don't like this economy.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌这种经济状况。

sentences.en: There's a lot of psychology to this.
sentences.zh: 这其中包含着很多心理因素。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Because with inflation, what you're seeing now makes you start to worry about what's going to happen in the future.
sentences.zh: 因为面对通货膨胀，你现在所看到的会让你开始担心未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: You see the prices that are going up right now, and you start to say, well, what if that continues?
sentences.zh: 你看到眼下正在上涨的物价，然后你就会开始想，嗯，如果这种情况持续下去会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm going to end up worse.
sentences.zh: 我最后的结果会变得更糟。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, somebody who might otherwise be pretty optimistic about the economy suddenly starts answering that survey question.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，一个原本对经济相当乐观的人，可能会开始这样回答调查问卷：

sentences.en: I feel pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 我感觉挺糟糕的。

sentences.en: I'm pretty pessimistic.
sentences.zh: 我相当悲观。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Okay, Ben, we're back.
sentences.zh: 好的，本，我们回来了。

sentences.en: We're in studio.
sentences.zh: 我们在演播室里。

sentences.en: It's still pretty exciting.
sentences.zh: 这依然让人觉得很兴奋。

sentences.en: You said, Ben, that there are two big reasons for the loss of confidence in the economy.
sentences.zh: 本，你刚才说，对经济失去信心有两个主要原因。

sentences.en: And inflation was the firSt. What is the second?
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀是第一个。第二个是什么？

sentences.en: So the second one is that nothing quite seems to be working right now.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因就是，现在好像没有什么事情是运转正常的。

sentences.en: You go to a store and
sentences.zh: 你去商店，

sentences.en: not all the products that you can usually get are there on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 平时能买到的产品并非全都在货架上。

sentences.en: Yeah, the shelves are sporadically bare.
sentences.zh: 对，货架时常空空如也。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now look, this is not you walk into a store and the shelves are empty.
sentences.zh: 现在听着，这并不是说你走进商店发现货架空空如也。

sentences.en: This isn't even like what we saw in the beginning of the pandemic where like you couldn't track down toilet paper
sentences.zh: 这甚至不像我们在大流行初期看到的那种情况，当时你在任何地方都

sentences.en: anywhere.
sentences.zh: 买不到卫生纸。

sentences.en: But I mean, the other day I went out to get butter for my wife to work on her wonderful pies.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，前几天我出去给我妻子买黄油，好让她做她拿手的馅饼。

sentences.en: And there was no butter at the corner store.
sentences.zh: 结果转角的小店里没有黄油。

sentences.en: Now look, I was able to go down to the other corner store and eventually I tracked down butter.
sentences.zh: 现在你看，我能够走到另一个转角的小店，最后总算找到了黄油。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I'm not used to going to the store and discovering that there's no butter.
sentences.zh: 但我并不习惯去商店却发现没有黄油。

sentences.en: No butter.
sentences.zh: 没有黄油。

sentences.en: And you're not going to use margarine.
sentences.zh: 而且你又不会去用人造黄油。

sentences.en: Oh, please.
sentences.zh: 哦，拜托。

sentences.en: Not for these pies.
sentences.zh: 做这些馅饼可不能用那个。

sentences.en: But that's happening all over the place.
sentences.zh: 但这种事到处都在发生。

sentences.en: Or you go online to buy something and it tells you it's backordered for six months or you can't get the color that you wanted or the type that you wanted.
sentences.zh: 或者你上网买东西，它告诉你缺货要等六个月，或者你买不到想要的颜色或想要的型号。

sentences.en: And so then you go out to eat at a restaurant and you've got a long wait and the, you know, server seems frazzled and the kitchen messes up your order and
sentences.zh: 接着你出去在餐馆吃饭，要等很久，而且服务员看起来心力交瘁，厨房把你的订单弄砸了，

sentences.en: you've got to bus your own plates.
sentences.zh: 你还得自己收拾盘子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Just in a lot of different ways, the level of service and the variety of products that we're used to getting are just not there right now.
sentences.zh: 总之在很多不同的方面，我们习惯享受的服务水平和产品种类，现在确实都不复存在了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Ben, as with inflation, I wonder if you can describe the person whose experience with this economic dysfunction is making them feel worse about the economy than perhaps they
sentences.zh: 那么，本，就像通货膨胀一样，我想知道你是否可以描述这样一个人：他们对这种经济功能失调的亲身经历，让他们对经济的感觉比他们

sentences.en: should if they're benefiting from higher wages, bigger savings, and so on.
sentences.zh: 在受益于更高工资、更多储蓄等等因素时本应感到的更加糟糕。

sentences.en: Let me give you a couple of examples.
sentences.zh: 我来举几个例子。

sentences.en: Take a parent with a young child.
sentences.zh: 以一个带着幼儿的父母为例。

sentences.en: We're in a major daycare crisis right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于严重的托儿危机中。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to find slots in daycare or it's very expensive when you can find one.
sentences.zh: 很难在托儿所找到名额，即便找到了也极其昂贵。

sentences.en: Because daycare is short-staffed.
sentences.zh: 因为托儿所人手不足。

sentences.en: Because daycare is short-staffed.
sentences.zh: 因为托儿所人手不足。

sentences.en: Because some daycare centers shut down in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因为一些托儿所在大流行期间倒闭了。

sentences.en: So you can imagine a family, maybe they have perfectly good jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象这样一个家庭，也许他们有非常不错的工作。

sentences.en: Maybe they're benefiting from that child tax credit that Congress passed that's helping them out.
sentences.zh: 也许他们正受益于国会通过的、对他们有所帮助的儿童税收抵免政策。

sentences.en: Financially, they may be doing okay right now.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，他们现在可能过得还不错。

sentences.en: But they are paying way more for daycare.
sentences.zh: 但他们为了托儿服务支付了高昂得多的费用。

sentences.en: Or maybe one of the parents actually has to stay home.
sentences.zh: 或者也许父母中的一方实际上不得不辞职回家。

sentences.en: Or maybe every three weeks, one of the parents gets a phone call saying, you've got to come pick up your kid because there's been an exposure and we're shutting down
sentences.zh: 或者也许每隔三周，父母就会接到一个电话，说：“你得来接你的孩子，因为有人接触过病例，我们要关闭

sentences.en: the daycare for the next week.
sentences.zh: 托儿所一周。”

sentences.en: And they miss work.
sentences.zh: 于是他们耽误了工作。

sentences.en: And they miss work.
sentences.zh: 于是他们耽误了工作。

sentences.en: There are direct financial consequences to that.
sentences.zh: 这会带来直接的经济后果。

sentences.en: But even aside from the direct financial consequences, it may just really not feel like things are working right now.
sentences.zh: 但抛开直接的经济后果不谈，人们可能真的会觉得现在事情都无法正常运转了。

sentences.en: When you can't even get stable daycare, something that many people could count on before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当连稳定的托儿服务都无法保证时——这可是大流行前许多人都可以指望的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: What's another example?
sentences.zh: 还有什么其他的例子吗？

sentences.en: Think about a restaurant worker.
sentences.zh: 想想餐厅服务员。

sentences.en: We were talking earlier about how restaurant workers are seeing these big wage increases.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才讨论过餐厅服务员的工资是如何大幅上涨的。

sentences.en: Well, the reason they're getting those wage increases is it's really hard to find workers right now, which means that pretty much every restaurant is horribly understaffed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们之所以能获得这些加薪，是因为现在真的很难找到工人，这意味着几乎每家餐厅都严重缺人。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, you're covering twice as many tables as usual, or you're covering twice as much on the line if you're in the kitchen than you used to.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你要负责两倍于平常的桌子，如果你在厨房工作，你要负责两条流水线的工作量。

sentences.en: You're getting yelled at by customers.
sentences.zh: 你遭到顾客的训斥。

sentences.en: You're being forced to enforce a mask mandate or a vax mandate.
sentences.zh: 你被迫去执行口罩强制令或疫苗强制令。

sentences.en: Your day-to-day life may be miserable.
sentences.zh: 你的日常生活可能会变得苦不堪言。

sentences.en: And sure, you're getting a couple bucks an hour more maybe than you were before.
sentences.zh: 当然，你的时薪可能比以前多了几块钱。

sentences.en: But that may not compensate you for how much worse your day-to-day existence is.
sentences.zh: 但这可能无法弥补你的日常生活变得多么糟糕。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: More money can only make you feel a certain level of happier with an economy if that economy
sentences.zh: 如果一个经济体日复一日、不断加深你对自己的糟糕感受，那么

sentences.en: is day in, day out, making you feel worse and worse about yourself.
sentences.zh: 更多的金钱也只能让你对这个经济体的满意度提升到某种程度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when we talk about this sort of contradiction, right, sometimes it can sound like we're saying,
sentences.zh: 当我们讨论这种矛盾时，有时听起来好像我们在说，

sentences.en: oh, well, you know, we know the economy is doing better if only stupid Americans understood how good the economy is right now.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，你知道，我们知道经济正在变好，要怪就怪那些愚蠢的美国人根本不明白现在经济有多好。

sentences.en: But that's not what we're talking about here, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们在这里讨论的不是这个，对吧？

sentences.en: We're talking about things being actually palpably worse for those workers and those consumers.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是这些工人和消费者确实感受到了切实更糟糕的处境。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So maybe, Ben, the word contradiction is not quite right at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，本，“矛盾”这个词也许根本就不太贴切。

sentences.en: It's not about good data, bad experience.
sentences.zh: 这无关美好的数据和糟糕的体验。

sentences.en: It's about perceptions and reality.
sentences.zh: 这关乎看法与现实。

sentences.en: And if your perception is that things are bad, then they're bad.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为事情很糟糕，那它就是很糟糕。

sentences.en: And no amount of, like, economic reality data is going to change that.
sentences.zh: 再多的经济现实数据也无法改变这一点。

sentences.en: That's not a contradiction.
sentences.zh: 这并不是矛盾。

sentences.en: That's people just feeling bad.
sentences.zh: 这只是人们实实在在的糟糕感受。

sentences.en: I mean, I think our data can only capture so much.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我们的数据能捕捉到的信息是有限的。

sentences.en: And it can both be true that in dollars and cents, most people are doing better now than they were a year ago or even better than they were before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 以下两点可以同时成立：从真金白银来看，大多数人现在的状况比一年前甚至比大流行之前还要好；

sentences.en: And at the same time, that for many people, life is not great right now.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，对许多人来说，眼下的生活并不美妙。

sentences.en: And those two things are not necessarily contradictory.
sentences.zh: 这两件事并不一定矛盾。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So I want to understand the implications of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想了解这背后的含义。

sentences.en: Maybe this is a naive question, but how important is it that a lot of people feel bad about the economy?
sentences.zh: 这也许是个幼稚的问题，但许多人对经济感到糟糕，这有多重要？

sentences.en: Is it something that we need to be all that worried about if the feelings are still a little bit untethered from the economic reality?
sentences.zh: 如果这种感受与经济现实还有些许脱节，这真的是我们需要全盘担忧的事情吗？

sentences.en: I know that might seem like I'm now contradicting myself because I just said, if your perception is bad, then it's bad.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来好像我正在自相矛盾，因为我刚说过，如果你的看法是糟糕的，那它就是糟糕的。

sentences.en: But maybe it's temporary.
sentences.zh: 但也许这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: So how big a deal is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这到底有多大关系？

sentences.en: So I think that temporary word is the critical one.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得“暂时”这个词才是关键所在。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Because the real question here is what happens over the next six, 12 months.
sentences.zh: 因为这里真正的问题是接下来六到十二个月会发生什么。

sentences.en: If you talk to people in the Biden White House right now, they are convinced that a year from now, the economy is not only going to be better, but it's going to feel better.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在跟拜登白宫的人谈谈，他们坚信一年后经济不仅会变得更好，而且人们的感觉也会更好。

sentences.en: Workers are going to come back as they feel better about the public health situation and probably as they run down some of the savings that they've built up
sentences.zh: 随着工人们对公共卫生状况感觉更好，并且可能会花掉他们积攒的一些存款，

sentences.en: and have to go back to work.
sentences.zh: 不得不重返工作岗位，工人们将会回归。

sentences.en: These supply chain shortages start to work themselves out, which we're already seeing some signs of.
sentences.zh: 这些供应链短缺问题开始自行解决，我们已经看到了一些迹象。

sentences.en: And we sort of look up in a little while, and this felt like this very strange moment that we all lived through.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿我们回过头来看，会觉得这只是我们共同经历过的一段非常奇怪的时期。

sentences.en: But the good stuff, the jobs and the wages, that's all still there.
sentences.zh: 但好的一面——工作和工资，这些都还在。

sentences.en: And all the stuff that was making us miserable, the inflation and the shortages and the understaffing.
sentences.zh: 而所有那些让我们痛苦不堪的东西，通货膨胀、短缺和人手不足……

sentences.en: Dissipates.
sentences.zh: 都消散了。

sentences.en: Dissipates.
sentences.zh: 都消散了。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, then we're going to be sitting here in a year and saying, look at how great the economy is.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那么一年后我们坐在这里就会说，瞧瞧经济有多棒。

sentences.en: If that's the case.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样的话。

sentences.en: If that's the case.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样。

sentences.en: If it's not the case.
sentences.zh: 如果不是这样呢。

sentences.en: So the risk here really is that the longer that this lasts, the more embedded it becomes.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的风险其实在于，这种情况持续的时间越长，它就越根深蒂固。

sentences.en: And this is especially true on the inflation question.
sentences.zh: 在通货膨胀的问题上尤其如此。

sentences.en: So we were talking before about how inflation is all about psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前在谈论通货膨胀全都是关于心理学的时候说过，

sentences.en: Well, if people see a price increase one day, that may be relatively easy to dismiss.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果人们某天看到物价上涨，这或许还相对容易忽视。

sentences.en: But as it goes on, people and businesses both start to say, well, this is just the reality we live in now.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，人们和企业都会开始说，好吧，这就是我们现在生活的现实。

sentences.en: So a retailer starts to raise prices because they assume that the products that they're selling are also going to go up in price.
sentences.zh: 因此，零售商开始提高价格，因为他们假设自己销售的产品价格也会上涨。

sentences.en: Or workers start going to their bosses and saying, have you seen what's going on with inflation?
sentences.zh: 或者员工开始去找老板说，你看到通货膨胀的情况了吗？

sentences.en: You've got to give me a raise.
sentences.zh: 你得给我加薪。

sentences.en: And then the company says, well, all right, we'll give you a raise.
sentences.zh: 然后公司说，好吧，我们会给你加薪。

sentences.en: But to cover that, we've got to raise prices.
sentences.zh: 但为了弥补这部分成本，我们必须提高价格。

sentences.en: Ah, in which case inflation.
sentences.zh: 啊，那样的话就会引发通货膨胀。

sentences.en: We get this cycle.
sentences.zh: 我们陷入了这种循环。

sentences.en: Feeds inflation.
sentences.zh: 助长了通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And once that happens, and I want to be clear, we do not see much evidence of that happening so far.
sentences.zh: 一旦这种情况发生——我想说明的是，到目前为止我们还没看到太多这种现象发生的迹象。

sentences.en: But once that happens, it becomes a very difficult cycle to break.
sentences.zh: 但一旦这种情况发生，这就成了一个非常难以打破的循环。

sentences.en: So that's why it matters.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这很重要。

sentences.en: The reason why it matters that people feel bad about the economy in this moment is that that psychology becomes normalized, built into the economy.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，人们对经济感觉不好之所以重要，是因为这种心理会变得正常化，并内化到经济中。

sentences.en: People respond to it in ways that actually make it even worse.
sentences.zh: 人们的反应实际上会使情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So if you are a policymaker right now, you're on the Fed, you're on the White House, what tools do you have to make this better?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你现在是一名决策者，你在美联储工作，或者在白宫工作，你有什么工具来改善这种情况？

sentences.en: Because it feels like specifically what we're talking about is fixing inflation, right?
sentences.zh: 因为感觉我们具体在讨论的是解决通货膨胀问题，对吧？

sentences.en: There's only so much anyone can do about the supply chain probleMs. And what you have identified as the biggest problem seems to be inflation.
sentences.zh: 对于供应链问题，大家能做的事情其实很有限。而你认为最大的问题似乎是通货膨胀。

sentences.en: So can it be solved in a relatively short period?
sentences.zh: 那么它能在相对较短的时间内得到解决吗？

sentences.en: So this is the thing that is so tricky.
sentences.zh: 这就是最棘手的地方。

sentences.en: Look, the Fed could control inflation.
sentences.zh: 听着，美联储是可以控制通货膨胀的。

sentences.en: But the way that they would control inflation is by slowing down the economy.
sentences.zh: 但他们控制通货膨胀的方式是通过放缓经济增长。

sentences.en: By raising, we've talked about this in the past, interest rates, making borrowing a little more expensive, therefore just kind of dampening things.
sentences.zh: 我们过去讨论过这一点，通过提高利率、增加借贷成本，从而给经济降温。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But at a moment when the economy is still getting back on its feet, when we still have 4 million fewer jobs than we did before the pandemic, the unemployment rate for
sentences.zh: 但在经济仍在恢复元气的时候，在我们比疫情前少400万个工作岗位的时候，黑人群体的失业率

sentences.en: black Americans right now is close to 8 percent.
sentences.zh: 目前接近8%。

sentences.en: There would be real consequences to slowing down the economy right now, potentially leading to people losing jobs, the unemployment rate going higher again.
sentences.zh: 现在让经济放缓会带来真正的后果，可能会导致人们失业，失业率再次上升。

sentences.en: That is not something that the Fed wants to do.
sentences.zh: 这不是美联储想做的事。

sentences.en: But they could do it.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实可以这么做。

sentences.en: They could do it.
sentences.zh: 他们是可以做到。

sentences.en: But they also want to make sure that the economy stays on its feet and they're trying to walk this very narrow line to try to get inflation under control, keep the recovery
sentences.zh: 但他们也希望确保经济保持复苏势头，他们正在走一条非常窄的钢丝，试图控制通货膨胀，保持复苏

sentences.en: on track, and we'll see how they do.
sentences.zh: 步入正轨，我们拭目以待他们的表现。

sentences.en: So for now, with the Federal Reserve Bank reluctant to take that action, we're going to be living in this weird economic moment for quite some time, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 所以就目前而言，由于美联储不愿采取行动，听起来我们在相当长的一段时间里都将生活在这种诡异的经济时刻中。

sentences.en: I think we know we're going to be dealing with a lot of these challenges into next year.
sentences.zh: 我想我们知道，在明年我们都将应对许多这样的挑战。

sentences.en: Beyond that, I think that's where we start to have real questions.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我认为我们才开始面临真正的疑问。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, we are all going to feel perhaps not so great about the economy, perhaps worse than we should on paper.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，我们对经济的感受可能不会太好，甚至可能比纸面上看起来的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: But I feel like the lesson of this interview, Ben, is that when it comes to the economy, the way we feel is everything.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉这次访谈给我们的教训是，本，当谈到经济时，我们的感受就是一切。

sentences.en: The way we feel is everything.
sentences.zh: 我们的感受就是一切。

sentences.en: Well, I feel this interview is over, and I want to thank you for being our inaugural
sentences.zh: 好吧，我觉得这次访谈结束了，我要感谢你成为我们恢复办公室线下访谈的第一位

sentences.en: return-to-office interview, Ben.
sentences.zh: 嘉宾，本。

sentences.en: It's been great being cooped up in a small padded office with you again, Michael.
sentences.zh: 再次和你一起被关在一个铺了软垫的小办公室里感觉真不错，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Yes, a small padded office with not that much ventilation.
sentences.zh: 是的，一个通风不太好的铺了软垫的小办公室。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So fun.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: Well, I guess that's it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想就这样了。

sentences.en: I guess the worst part of this all is I now have to walk you out of a studio, make small talk.
sentences.zh: 我想这一切中最糟糕的部分是，我现在得送你走出工作室，还得跟你客套闲聊。

sentences.en: The best part of it is just like, boop.
sentences.zh: 最棒的部分就像是，啵。

sentences.en: But we're done here.
sentences.zh: 但我们到此为止了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye, guys.
sentences.zh: 再见，各位。

sentences.en: I'm going to walk Ben out and make small talk with him.
sentences.zh: 我要送本出去，顺便跟他闲聊。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the House of Representatives narrowly voted to reprimand a Republican member of the
sentences.zh: 周三，众议院以微弱优势投票谴责了一名共和党众议员、

sentences.en: body, Congressman Paul Gosar of Arizona, and strip him of his committee assignments for posting an
sentences.zh: 来自亚利桑那州的保罗·戈萨尔（Paul Gosar）议员，并剥夺了他的委员会职务，因为他在网上发布了一段

sentences.en: animated video depicting him killing a Democratic colleague, Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and assaulting President Biden.
sentences.zh: 动画视频，其中描绘了他杀死民主党同僚、众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯（Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez），并袭击总统拜登的画面。

sentences.en: As leaders in this country, when we incite violence with depictions against our colleagues, that trickles down into violence in this country.
sentences.zh: 作为这个国家的领导人，当我们用针对同事的影像煽动暴力时，这种暴力就会渗漏到这个国家的各个角落。

sentences.en: And that is where we must draw the line independent of party identity or belief.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们必须划清界限的地方，无论党派身份或信仰如何。

sentences.en: Democrats, including Ocasio-Cortez, said they felt obligated to speak out against threats that
sentences.zh: 民主党人（包括奥卡西奥-科尔特斯）表示，他们觉得自己有义务大声疾呼，反对那些

sentences.en: could once again inspire the kind of violence that occurred on January 6th when supporters of President Trump stormed the U.S.
sentences.zh: 可能再次激起1月6日那类暴力的威胁。当时，特朗普总统的支持者冲击了美国

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦。

sentences.en: It is inconceivable that a member of our community here would wish to repeat the violence of that dark day, that deadly day.
sentences.zh: 我们社区的一名成员竟然希望重演那个黑暗日子、那个致命日子的暴力，这是不可想象的。

sentences.en: House Republicans, all but two of whom voted against the punishment, called the vote a partisan attempt to silence one of their own.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党人（除两人外其余均投票反对这一惩罚措施）称这次投票是压制异己党派企图。

sentences.en: For Democrats, this vote isn't about a video.
sentences.zh: 对民主党人来说，这次投票无关视频。

sentences.en: It's about control.
sentences.zh: 关乎控制。

sentences.en: That's the one and only thing Democrats are interested in.
sentences.zh: 那是民主党人唯一感兴趣的事情。

sentences.en: Not condemning violence, not protecting the institution, not decorum or decency, just control.
sentences.zh: 不是谴责暴力，不是保护机构，不是讲究礼仪或体面，只是为了控制。
